messages:
Sam K: Quick handoff — I'm out in 20m, leaving primary to Devon T. Short summary:
- Incident: intermittent p99 token latency spike on /v1/generate, started ~20m ago
- Impact: some production customers saw 502/timeout; retries increased, user-facing stalls
- What we tried: scaled up gen pool by +2 nodes, evicted suspicious pods, KV cache warmup
- Current signal: error rate down but p99 still elevated for long sequences
Actions I'm leaving:
1) Devon T: take primary. Watch traces in Console -> /routes/gen -> traces p99. If p99 > 1.5s for >5m, follow fallback plan.
2) Elyse: you're secondary, monitor incidentbot and escalate to eng-runtime if autoscaler doesn't respond.

IncidentBot: Pager: HIGH latency detected on /v1/generate (alert_id=INC-2026-1452) — p99=2.1s, error-rate=3.8% :rotating_light:

Devon T: ack. taking primary. hopping in now. Can you paste the runbook link? not seeing the KV-cache doc in quicklinks.

Sam K: runbooks — KV cache stall: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/kv-cache-stall | Gen-p99 mitigation: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/gen-p99-fallbacks
Quick pointers:
- Try a controlled rollout to model-quant (lower memory) via Console -> Deployments -> Rollout -> variant=quantized
- Short term: disable long-sequence batching: set route override `max_batch_seq`=512
- If autoscaler stuck: `kubectl get hpa -n inference gen-deployment` then `kubectl patch hpa ...` (see runbook)

Maria L: FYI support reported a customer facing increased latency on checkout flow, ticket #CS-4123

Devon T: on it. running quick health checks:
```
# check pod restarts
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=gen -o wide
# connect to pod and check kv cache mem
kubectl exec -n inference gen-0 -- bash -lc 'ps aux | grep runtime && du -sh /mnt/kvcache'
```

Elyse (Oncall): I'm watching logs and traces. If you need immediate fallback, enable `model_fallback=on` for route `prod/gen` (Console -> Route Overrides). That will route to smaller model and should bring p99 down under 1s.

IncidentBot: Note: autoscaler triggered scale-up 2m ago. New pods coming up.

Ash S: Quick note — if you do a rollback, prefer a canary rollback to the previous model version not to old config that had batching turned off. We had a regression last month when rolling to pre-2026-03 config.

Devon T: Thanks. I see one pod with elevated OOMKills in the last hour. Starting a rolling restart of the pod set now.
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/gen -n inference --timeout=300s
```

Sam K: good. handover checklist for you:
- Confirm new pods are Ready and passing /health
- Verify p99 back to <1s for 10m
- Post an update to #incidents with `status: monitoring` once stable
- If not stable after 15m, escalate to eng-runtime (pager on-call) and open an RCA ticket

Devon T: Doing health checks... new pods Ready=3/3. Health ok. p99 dropped to 0.92s in sampling. Monitoring for 10m. Will post update.

Maria L: I'll update CS with temp mitigation note: enabling model_fallback, possible degraded accuracy.

Elyse (Oncall): Also enabling extra tracing for a 30min window so we can collect spans.

Devon T: Update at 1768001400: p99=0.9s, error-rate=0.7%. Marking `status: monitoring` in #incidents. Leaving detailed notes in the incident doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-1452

Sam K: thanks team — Devon primary confirmed, Elyse secondary. I'm leaving now — ping me if anything flares. :thumbsup:

Ash S: one more: quick commands (copy/paste) if KV cache stall suspected:
```
# dump kv cache keys (careful in prod)
redis-cli -h kv-cache.prod.internal -p 6379 --scan | head -n 50
# clear prefix (use only if instructed)
redis-cli -h kv-cache.prod.internal -p 6379 --scan --pattern "route:prod/gen:*" | xargs -n 100 redis-cli -h kv-cache.prod.internal -p 6379 del
```

IncidentBot: Auto-close note: will mark alert as acknowledged if p99 stays <1s for 15m.

Devon T: closing thread in 30m unless anything else. Thanks all. :rocket:
